'''''Angelica pachycarpa''''', the '''Portuguese angelica''',<ref name=BSBI07>{{BSBI 2007 |accessdate=2014-10-17 }}</ref> is a [[herbaceous plant|herbaceous]] [[perennial plant|perennial]] plant native to north western Spain and western Portugal,<ref name="Méndez1973">{{citation| last1 = Méndez | first1 =  J.| year = 1973| title = Coumarins of Angelica pachycarpa| journal = Experientia | volume = 29| issue = 3| pages = 371–372| doi = 10.1007/BF01926538| pmid = 4708735| last2 = Rubido| first2 = J.| last3 = Mato| first3 = M. C.| s2cid = 20287729}}</ref> and naturalised in New Zealand.<ref name="nzpcn.org.nz">{{cite web |url=http://nzpcn.org.nz/flora_details.asp?ID=2537 |title=New Zealand Plant Conservation Network |website=nzpcn.org.nz |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100523040305/http://www.nzpcn.org.nz/flora_details.asp?ID=2537 |archive-date=2010-05-23}} </ref> It inhabits forests, grasslands and stream sides and is occasionally grown as an ornamental garden subject for its glossy foliage and umbels of white flowers.

==Distribution==
It is present in coastal regions of north western Spain from [[Santander, Spain|Santander]] west to the [[Portugal-Spain border]] and has a [[disjunct population]] in the [[Berlengas|Berlengas archipelago]] off central-western Portugal.<ref>{{cite web |title=Angelica L. |url=http://www.floraiberica.es/floraiberica/texto/pdfs/10_129_67%20Angelica.pdf |publisher=[[Flora Ibérica]] |accessdate=13 November 2020}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Angelica pachycarpa |url=https://flora-on.pt/#/1Angelica+pachycarpa |publisher=Flora-on |accessdate=13 November 2020}}</ref>

==Description==
''Angelica pachycarpa'' is a short-lived, stout fleshy plant. It grows about one meter tall, with very glossy dark green foliage. It has creamy-white to greenish-white flowers in flat umbels that are ten to twenty centimeters wide. The foliage and hollow stems have a faint [[anise]]ed odor.  The stems are grooved.  The base foliage is two to three [[pinnate]] and noticeable [[Petiole (botany)|petiolate]]; the stem leaves are one to three pinnate with very short petioles.  The fruit are up to twelve millimeters long, brown with lighter colored wings, and have a pepper-like scent.<ref name="nzpcn.org.nz" />

''Angelica pachycarpa'' is found growing in the Crithmo-Armerion maritimae (Géhu 1968) community of plants in Spain and Portugal which includes these species also: ''[[Armeria berlengensis]]'', ''Armeria euscadiensis'', ''[[Armeria maritima]]'' subsp. ''miscella'', ''Armeria pubigera'' subsp. ''depilata'', ''Armeria pubigera'' subsp. ''pubigera'', ''Centaurea borjae'', ''[[Daucus gingidium]]'' subsp. ''atlanticum'', ''[[Leucanthemum]] ircutianum'' subsp. ''crassifolium'', ''Leucanthemum merinoi'', ''Leucanthemum pluriflorum'', ''[[Rumex acetosa]]'' subsp. ''biformis'', ''Rumex rupestris'', ''Sesamoides suffruticosa'' subsp. ''latifolia'', ''[[Silene uniflora]]'', ''Spergularia rupicola'' subsp. ''rupicola'', ''[[Trifolium occidentale]]''.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.ucm.es/info/cif/book/addenda/addenda2_01.htm|title = Addenda to the Syntaxonomical checklist of Spain and Portugal [2_01]}}</ref>
